# Validate the 40,960 MiB cache-ram change on a live post-deploy window

Follow-up to the "Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB" item and to
LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW.

## Goal

After the 40,960 MiB cap has been deployed and a comparable post-deploy window
has been gathered, empirically confirm a positive impact versus the 32,768 MiB
window: evictions continue to fall (ideally to ~0) with no throughput or
client-visible first-byte latency regression.

## Blocked by

The raise item — this validation must not start until 40,960 MiB is live.
Waiting for the post-deploy window is expected (the 2026-10-12 verification
used ~4.7 d / 1,404 requests).

## Acceptance criteria

- Confirm the spawned Qwen3 child llama-server args include
   `--cache-ram 40960` and `--swa-checkpoints 32` (the `--ctx-checkpoints`
   alias — the observable arg at deploy, per docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md
   `40960 MiB deploy`), and no `--swa-full`.
- Capture a post-deploy measurement with
   `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --json --recommend --cache-ram-filter 40960`
   over a window comparable to the 32 GiB verification window (~4.7 d /
   1,404 requests) or longer, saved as a committed artifact.
- Evictions fall further versus the 32,768 MiB window (18 -> fewer),
   `tokens_prefilled`/req and forced full-prefills do not rise, and held
   prompts do not fall.
- `prompt_eval_tok_s`, `decode_tok_s` and `first_byte_ms` (proxy-side) do not
   regress versus the 32,768 MiB measurement.
- Record the before/after figures on this item and on LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW,
   and update `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`.

## Notes

- Control for the slot profile (the 3 -> 1 slot change, LP-0MU1S617L) and for
  window length; the 2026-10-12 verification found throughput/wall metrics
  confounded by those.
- Proxy logs rotate quickly; capture `first_byte_ms` over an aligned proxy
  glob at measurement time.
- If the cache still saturates at 40,960 MiB, record the new `--recommend`
  output rather than raising again in this item.

Discovered from: LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW

## Producer decisions and evaluation methodology (2026-10-16)

Producer answers to the interim-validation questions raised this session:

1. **Window sufficiency** — wait for the full window (do not close on the
   interim ~2.3 d / 1,065-request data).
2. **AC3/AC4 deltas** — wait for the full window before judging whether the
   apparent throughput/latency regressions are confounds or a real regression.
3. **Slot profile** — agent's call; the producer wants a clear answer on
   whether the larger cache works, with the evaluation separated by slot count.

### Agreed methodology (agent's call)

- Do **not** start the measurement until the window matures, i.e. until
  ~2026-10-18 ~16:20 UTC (~4.7 d after the 2026-10-13 23:31 UTC deploy).
- Capture the required aggregate artifact (AC2), then additionally partition
  the 40,960 MiB corpus by the Qwen3 child's slot count and run the analysis
  once per partition.
- The authoritative slot signal is the child's
  `srv load_model: initializing slots, n_slots = N` line (corroborated by the
  `--parallel N` spawn arg) in each llama-server log file — **not** the proxy's
  `total_slots` field, which mixes profiles and is unreliable.
- Report the 1-slot and 3-slot subsets separately, and give a clear verdict on
  whether the larger cache works.

### Known limitation for the slot-controlled comparison

The 32,768 MiB baseline's per-slot composition is **not** reconstructible: the
numbered llama-server log files that held the bulk of its 1,404 requests have
since been rotated away. Only ~164 requests of daily files survive, all
`n_slots = 1`, so the committed 32 GiB artifact remains aggregate-only
(`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`). The slot-split
evaluation can therefore be applied only to the new window; the baseline
reference is the committed aggregate.
data.title: Validate the 40,960 MiB cache-ram change on a live post-deploy window

# Slot sweep 1/2/3 with recorded results

Child of LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 (evaluate single slot count for fast/cheap modes).

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want a reproducible 1/2/3-slot benchmark sweep run at the
observed production concurrency with raw results committed, so the
single-slot-count verdict rests on measured numbers rather than estimates.

Covers parent acceptance criterion 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The extended harness is run for `session_slot_pool_size` N = 1, 2 and 3 on
- Covers LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 AC1: benchmark results for 1, 2 and 3 slots recorded with reproducible commands, configs and raw numbers, covering throughput, latency/TTFT, queue-timeout / fallback_after_queue rate, local stream share and local quarantine episodes, at the observed concurrency (2-3 concurrent sessions plus queue depth).
   the local Qwen3 backend, at >= the observed concurrency (2-3 concurrent
   sessions plus queue depth), with the exact command, config diff, model,
   context size and per-slot context recorded for each run.
- Each run records throughput, latency/TTFT, queue-timeout rate, local stream
   share and local quarantine episodes; GPU/system memory and observed
   per-slot context are recorded where available.
- Raw results (JSON plus the summary report) are committed under
   `proxy/benchmarks/` (or a documented results directory) and are sufficient
   for a third party to re-derive the comparison without re-running.
- Viability-failure signals are recorded, not hidden: OOM, llama-server
   failure to start at a given N, or a per-slot context reduction large enough
   to change routing behaviour.
- Any config edit made for benchmarking is reverted and the proxy is left
   running the correct scheduled mode at the end of the run; the restoration is
   evidenced in the work-item comment.
## Minimal implementation

- Run the extended harness for N = 1, 2, 3 (config swap via the harness's
  existing config-surgery path or an explicit documented override).
- Capture the surrounding proxy log window per run so the derived metrics are
  auditable.
- Commit the JSON artefacts plus a short results note (env, commands, caveats).

## Constraints

- The proxy serves concurrent production consumers: no permanent config drift,
  and the running mode must be correct at the end.
- Slot count must match llama-server `--parallel`; each N requires a
  llama-server restart (the cost under evaluation).
- Transient outputs must not leave tracked paths permanently dirty — commit the
  artefacts intentionally or document the output location.
- Benchmarking 3 x 262144 ctx may OOM or force a lower per-slot context; record
  memory and per-slot context, and treat OOM / severely reduced per-slot
  context as a viability failure.
- The benchmark workload may not match real traffic; characterise the request
  mix explicitly (see sibling child on local-eligible traffic) and state the
  fidelity caveat in the results note.

## Deliverables

- Committed benchmark artefacts (JSON + results note) for N = 1, 2, 3.
- A work-item comment recording the exact commands, config diffs and
  config-restoration evidence.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — extended harness to run
- `proxy/config.yaml` — base slot count and context size
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — 3-slot overlay
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — restart path used between slot counts
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — llama-server start/`--parallel` wiring

## Dependencies

Depends on the harness-extension child (contention metrics and concurrency
parameters must exist before the sweep can produce the required numbers).
data.title: Slot sweep 1/2/3 with recorded results

data.description:
## Goal

Make the proxy respect MunitoAI's `x-ratelimit-*` response headers so it
stops probing the endpoint with requests that are guaranteed to be rejected
during a rate-limit exhaustion window, computing a proper cooldown from the
upstream's own reset timing instead of blind exponential backoff.

## Context / evidence (discovered 2026-10-16, from analysis of
`/var/log/llama-proxy` over the preceding 48h)

- MunitoAI 429 responses carry `{"error":{"message":"Too Many Requests","type":"rate_limit_error","param":null,"code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}}`
  and **no standard `Retry-After` header**, only custom headers, e.g.:
  `x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 10`, `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 0`,
  `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 52s`, `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes`
  (plus input/output/token variants).
- The proxy does not read any `x-ratelimit-*` header (verified: no code
  paths parse them). `_parse_retry_after` only handles `Retry-After`, which
  Munito never sends.
- Result: during the 48h window the endpoint returned 532 distinct failures
  (480 HTTP errors: 450×429, 15×400, 12×503, 3×502; 52 connect/read/empty).
  Because each 429 lands in the generic `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`
  path (exponential backoff 1s→45s, capped at config
  `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60`), the proxy re-tries munitoai roughly every
  ≤45s during exhaustion — ~21,600 `Skipping provider=munitoai ... in
  cooldown` lines and repeated 429 bursts across the window, with traffic
  piling onto opencode-go-2 (388 falloffs). Munito's own reset header said
  52s on the live test request — far longer than the base 1s backoff.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: When a provider entry declares `respect_ratelimit_headers: true` (or
  the behaviour is enabled globally via `server.*` config), the proxy parses
  `x-ratelimit-reset-requests` / `x-ratelimit-reset-tokens` /
  `x-ratelimit-reset-input-tokens` / `x-ratelimit-reset-output-tokens` (and
  `x-ratelimit-over-limit`, if present) from an upstream HTTP 429 response.
- AC2: On a 429 with a parseable reset duration, the provider's cooldown is
  set to at least the reset duration (plus a small safety margin), replacing
  the pure exponential-backoff guess; per-provider failure counters are still
  respected so repeated failures extend the cooldown sensibly.
- AC3: On a 429 with `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes` but no parseable reset,
  the behaviour falls back to the current exponential backoff unchanged (no
  regression for providers that only send `Retry-After` or nothing).
- AC4: The resolved cooldown is surfaced in the attempt record
  (`cooldown_seconds`) and the `Skipping provider=... in cooldown (Ns
  remaining)` log line reflects the header-derived duration.
- AC5: Unit tests cover: header parsing (seconds + optional unit suffixes
  like `52s`, `1m`, `1h30m`), the `x-ratelimit-over-limit` flag, precedence
  over backoff, fallback when headers are absent, and persistence of the
  header-derived cooldown in provider-state.json.
- AC6: Backward compatible: munitoai and all existing providers behave
  identically when the new config/flag is not enabled (default off).

## Out of scope

- Changing MunitoAI's quota/plan or renegotiating limits upstream.
- Surfacing `x-ratelimit-*` headers to proxy clients (though doing so is
  a cheap follow-up that could be noted).

## Related

- discovered-from: LP-0MV5UPXKL002MSKB (Add MunitoAI to fallback chains),
  LP-0MV6ENYYH006XX0Z (promote munitoai tier after local Qwen)
data.title: Proxy: honour MunitoAI x-ratelimit-* headers when queuing 429 cooldowns
